title: Pizza Kitchen
strapline: Take the order, roll the dough, share it out.
intent: Making and sharing food is one of the most sociable, purposeful games there is, and pizza is a favourite children know well.
Rolling, stretching, sprinkling and cutting are a genuine fine-motor and hand-strength workout.
Sharing a pizza into equal slices is early fractions and fair-share thinking in the most natural setting.
Taking orders and serving builds real conversation and cooperation between cook, waiter and customer.
Ingredient names, order pads and menus pull in vocabulary, mark-making and counting.
implementation: Offer dough or playdough bases, and 'toppings' children can sort and add — beads, felt shapes, loose parts.
Take a customer or hungry-family role so children cook, serve and share the food out.
Model the kitchen talk: 'One large pizza with cheese and tomato — coming right up!'
Draw out fair sharing: 'There are four of us — how can we cut it so everyone gets the same?'
Leave order pads, a menu and a till so writing, reading and number all have a reason.
Add counting and sorting of toppings, and comparing whose pizza has more.
Where you can, make real dough or wraps so the cooking and sharing is genuine.
key_questions: What would you like on your pizza today?
How can we cut this so everyone gets a fair share?
How many pieces of sweetcorn should go on — can you count them out?
What will you write down so the chef gets the order right?
Whose pizza has more toppings — how can we check?

impact.text: Children roll, stretch, sprinkle and cut, strengthening hands and refining control.
Children share the pizza into equal pieces and talk about fairness and 'the same amount for everyone'.
Children count toppings and slices and compare amounts using real number talk.
Children take and give orders in role, cooperating between cook, waiter and customer.
Children write orders and read the menu, mark-making that carries a real message.
Children sort and choose toppings, grouping the ingredients as they build each pizza.

enhancements: Playdough or real dough, rolling pins and a blunt pizza cutter.
Sorted 'toppings': felt shapes, beads, buttons, loose parts in labelled tubs.
Order pads, a menu, a till and a phone for takeaway orders.
Pizza boxes (clean, from home) and a delivery bike or bag.
Paper plates and a real fair-share challenge for a family of different sizes.
A cooking session making real mini wraps or dough to bake.

playing_exploring: Children play at a warm, familiar activity and throw themselves into making and serving.
They explore the dough and toppings with all their senses.
active_learning: Children keep the kitchen running through orders and deliveries, seeing each pizza through.
creating_thinking: Children solve fair sharing, invent their own toppings and adapt to what each customer wants.
